- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% relative to prior trough.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% on day 2 post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates late-period (last 10 days) prices; cap forecast at 10% below true outcome’s final 5-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” (strong bullish) followed by “0.00” (neutral), model tends to overreact; apply 10–15% downward adjustment on day 3–5 after such pattern.
